clue.text: Sign of eagle, for instance, swallowing large, large snake

indicators.note: something that swallows takes other things down inside itself, so one piece goes round the rest

blocks.note: an eagle is one example of a bird
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
the same abbreviation used a second time
a boa is a big constricting snake

explanation.surface: An eagle seen gulping down a huge snake is taken as some kind of omen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign of eagle' reads as a portent, but 'Sign' alone is the definition and 'of' just links it. BIRD opens to take in L, L and BOA, giving BILLBOARD, the first of the puzzle's magazine titles.
explanation.definitionFit: A billboard is a large outdoor advertising hoarding, a kind of public sign.

clue.text: Start of dissent in youth organization

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter alone
one thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a boy is a youth
the first letter of dissent

explanation.surface: The first signs of rebellion appear in a group for young people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Youth organization' reads as one phrase like the Scouts, but 'youth' is wordplay and 'organization' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A body is an organized group, such as a governing body, so it is a synonym for organization.

clue.text: Glib rationalization concealing a sign

indicators.note: something concealing an item holds it out of sight within its letters

blocks.note: found running across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: A slick excuse hides some telltale clue to the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra, the scales, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Maliciously ruin a lab in stereo

indicators.note: ruining something wrecks its form, so the letters that follow are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
the verb doubles as fodder as well as signalling the change

explanation.surface: A saboteur wrecks a laboratory while music plays through stereo speakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maliciously' tells you to rearrange, and 'ruin a lab' supplies all eight letters, so 'ruin' does double duty in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Binaural sound uses two channels, one for each ear, so it is heard in stereo.

clue.text: Puzzle's row missing the first letter

indicators.note: missing a letter means it is dropped, and the opening one is specified

blocks.note: to paddle a boat is to row it

explanation.surface: A line in a crossword is short one letter at its start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puzzle's row' suggests a line of a crossword; the apostrophe-s only means 'is', and 'row' is the oar-driven verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To addle someone is to confuse or muddle them, which is what puzzling them does.

clue.text: British pop singer accomplished nothing

blocks.note: did, past tense of do, means accomplished
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a British pop star's career.
explanation.definitionFit: Dido is an English singer known for hits such as 'Thank You' and 'White Flag'.

clue.text: Excited, I drew sloppily

indicators.note: work done sloppily comes out disordered, so the letters before it get jumbled

blocks.note: the five letters of these two words are the fodder

explanation.surface: An over-eager artist dashes off a careless sketch in a state of excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: Wired is slang for keyed-up or overstimulated, a synonym of excited; it is also a magazine title.

clue.text: Trendy humor bestseller

blocks.note: wit is clever humor
a hit is a big commercial success

explanation.surface: A fashionable comic book tops the bestseller lists.
explanation.definitionFit: With-it is informal for fashionable and up to date, the same as trendy.

clue.text: Inn where I spilled Riesling, for example

indicators.note: spilled contents end up scattered, so the preceding letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; the whole phrase is fodder

explanation.surface: A drinker remembers the pub where they knocked over a glass of German white.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inn where I' is all fodder; 'where' looks like a joining word but its letters are needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Riesling is a grape variety grown along the Rhine, and wine from that region is called Rhine wine.

clue.text: Exhume diner? It's disgusting

indicators.note: something disgusting is foul and messed up, so the letters are messed up too

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone recoils at the idea of digging up a restaurant patron.
explanation.definitionFit: To disinter is to dig up a buried body, exactly what exhuming means.

clue.text: Young socialite, lacking depth, prepared chicken

blocks.note: a deb (debutante) is a young woman entering society
something one-D (one-dimensional) has no depth

explanation.surface: A shallow young society girl is cooking chicken for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking depth' reads as an insult to the socialite, but it is wordplay: something one-dimensional, written ONE-D, has no depth.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken readied for cooking by having its bones removed is described as deboned.

clue.text: Specifies: "Delta is flying"

indicators.note: things sent flying land scattered in a new order

blocks.note: the airline name plus the next word supply the letters

explanation.surface: Someone booking travel states plainly which airline will be used: Delta.
explanation.definitionFit: To detail something is to set it out item by item, which is what specifying means; Details was also a magazine.

clue.text: Quality of tarnished tea urn

indicators.note: a tarnished thing is spoiled from its first state, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone judges the condition of an old, discoloured urn used for serving tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Nature can mean the essential character or quality of a thing; Nature is also a science journal.

clue.text: City creature and farm animal one gets mixed up

indicators.note: being mixed up means put out of order, so the preceding word's letters are jumbled

blocks.note: a pig is a typical farmyard animal
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An urban animal and a farmyard animal are confused for one another.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigeons are the birds most associated with city streets and squares.

clue.text: Appears onstage in a remake of Cats

indicators.note: a remake reworks the original into a new version, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: the Lloyd Webber musical's title supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A performer takes the stage in a new production of the musical Cats.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who acts is performing, which means appearing onstage in a role.

clue.text: Surreal act incorporating Latin translation for "ocean"

indicators.note: something surreal is distorted from normal reality, so the letters are distorted too
a translation renders words into a different form, here a different letter order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dreamlike stage act includes giving the Latin word for 'ocean'.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites you to think of the Latin word for ocean; instead the letters of ACT and LATIN together are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atlantic is one of the world's great oceans; The Atlantic is also a magazine.

clue.text: Dither aimlessly about someone who's dishonorable and mediocre

indicators.note: moving aimlessly means wandering without order, so the letters wander
about means around, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: the six letters to be rearranged
a rat is a treacherous, dishonorable person

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates pointlessly over a scoundrel who is also second-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Third-rate means of poor, inferior quality, a stronger form of mediocre.

clue.text: Big fuss in Ecuador: everything is part of a list?

blocks.note: first meaning: a commotion or flap
second meaning: the Spanish word for everything, as spoken in Ecuador
third meaning: as in a list of tasks still to be done

explanation.surface: A huge commotion in Ecuador turns out to be just one item on someone's checklist.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: a fuss, the Spanish for 'everything' (Spanish is Ecuador's language), and the word before 'list' in a list of chores.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-do is a commotion, and a to-do list holds tasks pending, so each item belongs to it.

clue.text: Season or seasoning, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken sound, so the herb is only matched by pronunciation

blocks.note: thyme is a culinary herb used to season food

explanation.surface: A cook can't decide whether it's the time of year or the spice being talked about.
explanation.definitionFit: A season is a period of the year, and time can mean such a period, as in 'at this time of year'; Time is also a magazine.

clue.text: Lightened sausage hash with last bit of mustard

indicators.note: a hash is a chopped-up mix, so the letters are chopped and mixed
the last bit of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of mustard

explanation.surface: A lower-fat sausage hash is served with a dab of mustard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lightened' sounds like a diet version of the dish, but it is the definition, in the sense of easing a burden.
explanation.definitionFit: To assuage pain or worry is to ease it, so assuaged means lightened, as a load or a sorrow is.

clue.text: Cousin captivates Jennifer Lopez up north of Arizona with smooth music

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top
in a down entry, north of means placed directly above the next piece
to captivate is to hold captive, so one piece holds the others inside it

blocks.note: coz is an old short form of cousin
J.Lo is the singer's well-known nickname
AZ is the US postal code for Arizona

explanation.surface: A relative is charmed by J.Lo singing above some mellow tunes from the Southwest.
explanation.walkthrough: Coz is Shakespeare-era shorthand for cousin. In a down clue 'north of' means placed above, so the reversed singer sits directly before the state code, all held in the cousin.
explanation.definitionFit: Cool jazz is a relaxed, restrained style of jazz from the 1950s, so it is smooth music.

clue.text: Bites back in turn

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: nips are small bites

explanation.surface: Someone bitten retaliates by biting the other person in their turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bites back' looks like retaliation; it is a word for bites written backwards, with 'in' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin is a rotating movement, so it is a synonym of turn; Spin is also a music magazine.

clue.text: Track down ugly divorces

indicators.note: something ugly is misshapen, so the letters of the next word lose their shape

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A private investigator is hired to dig into messy, acrimonious marital break-ups.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover something is to find it after searching, which is what tracking it down means; Discover is a science magazine.

clue.text: Surprisingly at first, fish walk

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the first letter of surprisingly
to troll is to fish by trailing a line behind a boat

explanation.surface: Startlingly, a fish starts to walk on land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish' reads as a noun, but it is the verb: trolling is fishing with a trailed line.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroll is a leisurely walk, and to stroll is to walk at an easy pace.

clue.text: Modernize cute topless case for BlackBerry, say

indicators.note: without a top means the first letter of that word is removed
a case holds something, so these letters wrap around the device

blocks.note: taken as written before losing its head
a BlackBerry is an example of a PDA, a personal digital assistant

explanation.surface: Someone wants to refresh the look of their phone with a stylish, revealing cover.
explanation.walkthrough: CUTE without its first letter is UTE, which holds PDA. A BlackBerry was a popular PDA-style smartphone.
explanation.definitionFit: To update something is to bring it up to current standards, the same as making it modern.

clue.text: Laurel's offbeat attraction

indicators.note: something offbeat is unconventional, so the letters come out in an unconventional order

blocks.note: the six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The appeal of Stan Laurel, of Laurel and Hardy, lies in his quirky comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Allure is the power of attracting or charming, a synonym for attraction; Allure is also a beauty magazine.

clue.text: In a weekday, the end of partying

blocks.note: taken as written
Mon is the short form of Monday
the end of partying is its last letter

explanation.surface: On a working day, the celebrations wind down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a weekday' reads as one phrase, but 'In' alone is the definition, and the rest builds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Among means in the midst of or surrounded by, so it can stand in for 'in', as in 'among friends'.

clue.text: Quit eliminating last of enemies and be king

indicators.note: eliminating something removes it, so one letter is taken out
the last of a word is its final letter, which is the one to go

blocks.note: to resign is to quit a post
the last letter of enemies

explanation.surface: A ruler stops fighting off foes and simply rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last of' points to the final letter of enemies, which is the letter removed from the word for quit.
explanation.definitionFit: To reign is to rule as a monarch, which is what being king means.

clue.text: Unit leader of goats and sheep

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: the first letter of goats
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: One animal heads a mixed flock of goats and sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unit leader' looks like a commanding officer; 'Unit' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A gram is a metric measure of mass, one of the standard units of weight.

clue.text: God's canal flowing uphill

indicators.note: in a down entry, flowing uphill means running bottom to top, so the letters go backwards

blocks.note: the Suez Canal links the Mediterranean and the Red Sea

explanation.surface: A miraculous waterway runs uphill against nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'God's canal' suggests a divine waterway; the apostrophe-s means 'is', so the definition is 'God' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeus is the king of the gods in Greek mythology.

clue.text: Girl's surface love for the French charisma

indicators.note: a surface is the outside of something, so only the outer letters are kept

blocks.note: the outside letters of girl
amour is French for love

explanation.surface: A girl's superficial love affair with French culture gives her a certain allure.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamour is an exciting, magnetic attractiveness, close in meaning to charisma; Glamour is also a fashion magazine.

clue.text: In Old English, "Bristol" means "jewel-like"

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: OE is the standard abbreviation for Old English
Bristol Palin, daughter of the politician Sarah Palin

explanation.surface: A note on etymology claims a word meaning 'Bristol' in Old English meant 'jewel-like'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bristol' looks like the English city, but here it is Bristol Palin, the daughter of 2008 US vice-presidential candidate Sarah Palin; her surname sits inside OE.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaline describes something resembling opal, a gemstone, so it means jewel-like.

clue.text: Stay and succeed without oxygen

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the element named next is removed from the phrase

blocks.note: to do well is to succeed
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Advice for a climber at altitude: stay put, and manage to thrive without bottled oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: DO WELL loses its O to give the answer, which is also Dwell, a design magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to live or remain there, a synonym of stay.

clue.text: Amazing transformation outside of Everglades produces 11 of the Across entries

indicators.note: a transformation changes the shape of something, so its letters take a new order
the outside of a word is its first and last letter only

blocks.note: taken as written
the outer letters of the Florida swamp's name

explanation.surface: A dramatic change around the edges of the Everglades yields eleven of the puzzle's answers.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme: eleven across answers are magazine titles, from Billboard and Wired to Glamour and Dwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleven across answers here, such as Time, Nature and Wired, are names of periodicals, so they are all magazines.
